name: Portable propane heater (Buddy type and catalytic)

fuels: propane (1 lb disposable cylinders, or a 20 lb cylinder kept outdoors on a hose with filter)
combustion.note: Outdoor only in Canada: the Canada-sale Buddy manual says never in a home, camper, tent or car. US-sale manuals allow indoor use only in the enclosures and with the fresh-air opening on their label, never while sleeping, and emergency indoor use only on a 1 lb cylinder. Read the label.

comps.spec: 1 lb (16.4 oz) disposable propane cylinders, often several part-used ones nearby; a Buddy runs 3-6 h on one, and run times fall significantly below about -7 °C (20 °F)
comps.loc: Screwed into the side or back, and in the box or bag with it

comps.spec: Disposable 1 lb cylinders with the No. 600 valve thread; a refillable cylinder (20 lb at most) on a hose has to stay outdoors, and the US manual allows that set-up only for recreational or temporary construction work enclosures

Hose to a cylinder of 20 lb at most, usually with a disposable inline fuel filter (Mr. Heater F273699) that traps oil from the hose and is replaced annually; the Buddy-series hose F273704 needs no filter
Thermocouple of the ODS pilot (Buddy) or of the catalytic pad (Olympian: at least 15 mV when hot)
comps.loc: At the pilot beside the burner tile, or on the pad

comps.spec: Piezo spark igniter and electrode at the pilot
Gas control valve held open by the thermocouple, with a built-in regulator fixed at 11 in water column (about 2.7 kPa)
Tip-over switch that shuts the gas off when the heater is knocked or tipped
Polished reflector behind the burner, and the front wire guard
comps.loc: Behind and in front of the burner tile

buildings.loc: Heating and camping aisles; cylinders in the cage outside
Shelves with camping and ice-fishing gear
Trailers, cabins and the camp store
Parts counter; catalytic heaters fitted in trailers

notes: In Canada treat every Buddy-type heater as outdoor only: Mr. Heater's Canada-sale manual says outdoor use only and never in a home, camper, tent or car, and its FAQ says Canada does not allow propane heaters indoors (Mr. Heater MH9BX CAN, Mr. Heater FAQ). The US-sale Portable Buddy manual allows emergency indoor use only on a 1 lb cylinder, and recreational or commercial enclosures with a window or roof vent, with a 58 cm² (9 sq in) vent opening (116 cm², 18 sq in, for the Big Buddy), never while sleeping and not in a California dwelling (Mr. Heater MH9BX, Mr. Heater MH18B). A 20 lb cylinder on a hose stays outdoors and is allowed only for recreational or temporary work enclosures; Mr. Heater recommends one for continuous running below about -7 °C (20 °F) (Mr. Heater MH9BX). The heater can shut itself off when the room is short of fresh air and above about 2,100 m (7,000 ft), and catalytic pads are ruined by sprays, dust and cooking fumes (Mr. Heater MH9BX, Camco Wave). The maker manuals say not to subject a cylinder to excessive heat (Remington GFA, Deere HR-18R).
